title: GET https://api-ar-gc.bistudio.com/game-config/api/v1/reforger/<clientVersion>/<build>/list
$comment: Observed on 1.8.0.13 as the server's very first backend call, four times: 200, 4667-4668 bytes. It answers the online game config - the settings and the service status the server then works with. No request body: the version and the build are in the path. This call failing is what a server without a usable backend retries every ~6 seconds, logged as `[RestApi] ID:[1] TYPE:[GameConfig/List] ENV:[invalid] Error - Cannot send request`.

name.description: The game's short name. Observed: Reforger.

version.description: The version this config is for; the captured answers say 1.8.0 while the path says 1.8.0/13.

env.description: Capitalised environment name, `Production` in the captures - the same environment the REST log prints lowercase as `ENV:[production]`.

overview.description: The overall service state. In the captures there is no tag, status is `ok`, the message is empty and there is no health-check URL.

properties.description: Key/value pairs the game reads instead of hardcoding them - 42 of them in the captured answer, including the Link_* URLs the main menu opens.

name.description: Observed: Link_Bohemia, Link_Feedback, Link_Workshop and the rest of the Link_* family the binary also carries, plus the URI_* context names.

type.description: The declared type of the value. Only `string` was observed in the 42 entries.

value.description: The value. **Optional**: the captured answer has one entry, URI_StarRiver, with no value key at all - a context the client is told the name of without being given an address.

services.description: The per-service status list behind the game's `Arma Reforger Online Service(s) Status` screen - four entries in the capture: game-api, game-config and two more.

tag.description: The service's short name: `game-api` in the captured entry.

healthCheckUrl.description: A URL on the service's own host; 48 characters in the captured entry.

createdAt.description: When this config was published, 34-35 characters. It changes between runs, so the two captured answers differ in this field alone.

tag.description: The service tag, or null for the overview entry.

status.description: `ok` in every captured entry. Other values exist (`maintenance` and the like) but were not observed - compare the EServiceStatus names in the binary.

message.description: Empty when the service is healthy.

healthCheckUrl.description: Present on the individual services, null on the overview.
